title_insect_mouth: INSECT STING IN MOUTH OR THROAT
cpr_desc: Place hands in the center of the chest. Push hard and fast at a depth of 5-6 cm.
cpr_full_guidance: 1. Place hands in the center of the chest. 2. Lock your elbows straight. 3. Compress hard and fast to a depth of 5-6 cm at 110 BPM. 4. After 30 compressions give 2 rescue breaths, or continue hands-only compressions.
cpr_full_guidance_spoken: Step one: Place your hands in the center of the chest. Step two: Lock your elbows straight. Step three: Push hard and fast to a depth of five to six centimeters in rhythm with the metronome. Step four: After thirty compressions give two rescue breaths, or continue hands-only chest compressions without stopping.
choking_desc: Lean the patient forward. Deliver up to 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades. If ineffective, deliver up to 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver).
choking_desc_spoken: Step one: Lean the patient firmly forward. Step two: Deliver up to five sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Step three: If ineffective, stand behind them and perform up to five abdominal thrusts, the Heimlich maneuver. Step four: If the person collapses, call nine one one or one one two immediately and start C P R.
bleeding_desc: Apply immediate, direct pressure to the wound with a sterile dressing or clean cloth. Elevate the injured limb above heart level if possible. Do not remove soaked dressings — add more layers on top.
bleeding_desc_spoken: Step one: Apply immediate, firm pressure directly onto the wound with a clean cloth or sterile dressing. Step two: Elevate the injured limb above heart level if possible. Step three: Never remove soaked dressings, add fresh layers directly on top. Step four: For severe arterial bleeding, call nine one one or one one two immediately.
unconscious_desc: Open the airway by tilting the head back and lifting the chin. Check for normal breathing for 10 seconds (look, listen, feel). If breathing normally — place in the recovery position. If not breathing — begin CPR immediately.
unconscious_desc_spoken: Step one: Open the airway by gently tilting the head back and lifting the chin. Step two: Check for normal breathing for ten seconds by looking, listening, and feeling. Step three: If breathing normally, place them in the recovery position on their side. Step four: If they are not breathing normally, call nine one one or one one two and start C P R immediately.
guidance_fall_head_trauma: 1. Do not move abruptly; support head and neck. 2. Call 112/911 immediately if: loss of consciousness, vomiting, lethargy, or extreme drowsiness occurs. 3. Apply a cold compress to the bump. 4. Closely monitor behavior for 24 hours.
guidance_fall_head_trauma_spoken: Step one: Do not pick up or move the child abruptly, carefully stabilize the head and neck. Step two: Immediately call nine one one or one one two if there is any loss of consciousness, repeated vomiting, limpness, or abnormal drowsiness. Step three: Apply a cold compress wrapped in a cloth to reduce swelling. Step four: Closely monitor the child's alertness and behavior for the next twenty-four hours.
guidance_chemical_ingestion: 1. DO NOT induce vomiting to prevent airway foaming and burns. 2. Call 112 immediately and keep the container. 3. Rinse mouth with water. 4. Keep sitting upright and monitor breathing.
guidance_chemical_ingestion_spoken: Step one: Absolutely do not induce vomiting! This risks chemical foaming, severe airway burns, and aspiration into the lungs. Step two: Call nine one one or one one two immediately and secure the original container. Step three: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with clean water to remove any residual liquid or gel. Step four: Keep the person sitting upright and continuously monitor their breathing.
guidance_insect_mouth: 1. Call 112/911 immediately – sting in mouth risks rapid airway obstruction! 2. Give ice cubes to suck on or cold water. 3. Keep patient sitting upright. 4. Be ready for CPR.
guidance_insect_mouth_spoken: Step one: Call nine one one or one one two immediately! A sting inside the mouth or throat can cause complete airway blockage within sixty seconds! Step two: Give ice cubes to suck on or small sips of ice water to slow down internal swelling. Step three: Keep the patient sitting straight upright. Step four: Closely monitor their breathing and be ready to begin C P R.
guidance_insect_skin: 1. Scrape off the stinger with a card or fingernail. 2. Apply a cold compress. 3. Monitor for breathing difficulty or swelling – if present, call 112 immediately.
guidance_insect_skin_spoken: Step one: Scrape the stinger off sideways using a credit card edge or fingernail. Never pinch with tweezers as this injects remaining venom. Step two: Apply a cold compress to reduce pain and swelling. Step three: Watch closely for hives, facial swelling, or breathing difficulty. If observed, call nine one one or one one two immediately.
guidance_burn: 1. Cool with cold running tap water for 15-20 minutes. 2. Remove jewelry before swelling starts. 3. Cover loosely with a sterile dressing. 4. Do not pop blisters.
guidance_burn_spoken: Step one: Immediately cool the burn under clean, cool running tap water for a full fifteen to twenty minutes. Step two: Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing right away before severe swelling develops. Step three: Cover the burn loosely with a clean, sterile dressing. Do not pop blisters or apply ointments. Step four: For extensive burns or facial burns, call nine one one or one one two immediately.
guidance_seizure: 1. Protect head from injury (place something soft underneath). 2. DO NOT insert anything into mouth and do not restrain. 3. After shaking stops, place in recovery position and call 112.
guidance_seizure_spoken: Step one: Protect the head from trauma by placing a folded jacket or soft item underneath. Step two: Do not put anything between the teeth and do not forcefully restrain the convulsive movements. Step three: Clear away sharp or dangerous nearby objects. Step four: After convulsions stop, check breathing, turn the person into the recovery position, and call nine one one or one one two.
guidance_fracture: 1. Immobilize the injured limb in the position found (including adjacent joints). 2. Apply a cold compress wrapped in cloth. 3. Do not attempt to realign bone. 4. Proceed to emergency department or call 112.
guidance_fracture_spoken: Step one: Immobilize the injured limb exactly in the position you found it, supporting both the joint above and below the injury. Step two: Apply a cold compress wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling and pain. Step three: Do not attempt to straighten or realign the bone. Step four: Safely transport the patient to an emergency department or call nine one one or one one two.
guidance_nosebleed: 1. Lean the person slightly forward (never tilt back). 2. Firmly pinch the soft part of the nose for 10 minutes. 3. Apply a cold pack to the back of the neck. 4. Do not let them blow their nose.
guidance_nosebleed_spoken: Step one: Lean the person slightly forward. Never tilt the head back, as blood will enter the throat and stomach. Step two: Firmly pinch the soft fleshy part of the nose for ten uninterrupted minutes. Step three: Place a cold pack on the back of the neck or forehead. Step four: Do not allow the person to blow their nose after the bleeding stops.
guidance_general_emergency: 1. Ensure the scene is safe. 2. Check responsiveness and breathing. 3. In any medical emergency, call 112 immediately.
guidance_general_emergency_spoken: Step one: Ensure your own safety and that the scene is secure. Step two: Check if the person responds and assess their breathing. Step three: In any acute medical emergency, call nine one one or one one two immediately.
privacy_intro: This policy explains how information is handled when using the Emergency First Aid Dashboard.
privacy_body_one: The dashboard is designed to provide rapid first aid guidance and does not collect or store personal medical records.
privacy_body_two: Anonymous operational telemetry and performance cookies (Google Analytics 4 / GTM) may be used strictly to evaluate interface response times and system stability during emergencies.
terms_intro: These terms describe the intended use of the LifeLine Voice Emergency First Aid Dashboard.
terms_body_one: This interface provides automated first aid guidance for emergency situations. It does not replace professional emergency dispatchers or certified medical professionals.
terms_body_two: In any life-threatening emergency, immediately call your local emergency services (112 in the EU) and follow the instructions of emergency operators.
